artifacts.summary: Full 5-phase research for the HOLD task-status marker: confirms the live consumer-repo breakage (12 validate-state.sh FAILs, generate-todo.sh hard-fail) that Phase 1 fixes, maps every file/line the dispatch names, resolves the lift-surface and held-subtask-blocking design questions, and flags a pre-existing (out-of-scope) orchestrate.md STAGE 0 forced-terminal-admission gap that the new hold guard must not silently copy.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, the 'forced_round_complete)' case arm in the bucketing switch (pushes a reasoned blocked[] row via out_blocked_rows+=(...) and continues BEFORE the lock probe/dispatch_seq mint/status write) is the reusable precedent for adding any new non-dispatch-but-visible-reason status bucket to /orchestrate. Mirror this shape rather than inventing a new top-level excluded[] array -- blocked[] already carries 'no-defect-just-a-rule' reasons and needs no schema change downstream.

This codebase's convention for a projectEntry schema field that is valid only in one task status (e.g. completion_summary, 'required when status is completed... schema-optional here since only completed entries carry it') is to OMIT the key entirely when not applicable, never to set it to null. When a status like hold is lifted/reversed, clearing its associated fields should use jq del(...) rather than nulling them, to stay consistent with this existing pattern and with additionalProperties:false schema semantics.

commands/orchestrate.md's STAGE 0 validated_tasks loop unconditionally skips any completed|abandoned|expanded task without ever checking $FORCE_PHASES_FLAG, even though that variable is already populated at that point in the script. This appears to contradict the same file's own documented claim (lines ~59-61) that --research/--plan/--implement admit a terminal (even archived) task -- that admission machinery (task_has_forced_phase/effective_group) lives entirely inside orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, which the live dispatch path never reaches for a task STAGE 0 already dropped. Only the --dry-run path (which forwards raw, unfiltered $TASK_NUMBERS) actually exercises the forced-terminal-admission logic. Pre-existing gap, confirmed by reading the code, not yet fixed as of this finding.
